subject: Private endpoint egress: definitive IPs + SNI fingerprint acceptance
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@acmecorp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme NetOps <netops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private endpoint egress — definitive IPs + SNI fingerprint acceptance

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our Security/NetOps team needs a compact, signed acceptance packet we can hand to the firewall team. Specifically we need: 
- A definitive list of outbound IPs (single-IP or tight /32 ranges preferred) that our perimeter firewall must allow to reach the Redwood private control plane and telemetry endpoints.
- Any SNI/TLS fingerprinting guidance (SNI values, expected TLS server names, and whether we should pin SNI or rely on FQDN allowlisting).
- A short statement of fallback behaviour: what happens if our firewall blocks the control plane (retry/backoff, graceful degrade of inference, metrics exported).

I've attached our template (acme-egress-requirements.docx). Can you return a completed packet we can use for approval? Timebox: we need sign-off from Infrastructure by EOD next Thursday.

Rajesh Kumar
Network Engineering Lead, AcmeCorp
rajesh@acmecorp.com
Attachment: acme-egress-requirements.docx
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Acme NetOps <netops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — definitive IPs + SNI fingerprint acceptance

Rajesh — thanks for the clear checklist. Attaching a draft packet for your team to validate. Highlights up front:
- We can provide a stable set of four IPv4 /32 addresses for control-plane egress and two IPv4 /32 addresses for telemetry/metrics ingestion. See redwood-egress-ip-proposal.csv attached.
- We recommend allowlisting by IP for the control plane (fastest path for firewall teams). For higher security, we support SNI-based inspection: SNI hostnames are controlplane.private.redwood.ai and telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai.
- Fallback: if the control plane is unreachable, requests fall back to the nearest compatible model variant in-region with degraded telemetry (local caching will serve recent KV entries for up to 30s) — calls return 503 with Retry-After after aggressive backoff. Full behavior documented in the attached acceptance packet.

Could Karthik confirm the ephemeral/evolution policy on those IPs (rotation window, announced notice window) and Soojin confirm the evidence we should provide for Acme's compliance review?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood-egress-ip-proposal.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Acme NetOps <netops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 18:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — definitive IPs + SNI fingerprint acceptance

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from infra/runtime: 
- IPs: we can lock the four control-plane /32s for the initial GA period. We may offer ephemeral secondary pools for burst capacity; those will be behind the same DNS names and will be announced with a 48hr notice when we change ranges.
- TLS/SNI: we publish an authoritative SNI list but do not recommend strict SNI pinning for production unless you also allow the IPs; pinning can break during CA rotations. If Acme requires pinning, we can provide a short-lived certificate fingerprinting bundle (SHA256) and an operations playbook for rotation windows.
- Ports: outbound 443 only; telemetry uses TLS over 443 to telemetry.ingest.redwood.ai. No other outbound ports required.
- Health-check/metrics endpoints: 2x /32 used for passive ingestion; those IPs will be rate-limited from our side.

I'll put the final IP allocation into the proposal CSV (done) and add notes about rotation policy. Soojin, please advise on the evidence bundle we should include (SOC2 doc excerpt, recent penetration test summary, network flow samples, signed attestation).

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: egress-allowlist-snippets.txt
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Acme NetOps <netops@acmecorp.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — definitive IPs + SNI fingerprint acceptance

Appreciate the draft — security review notes below: 
- Evidence bundle we will attach: SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted), a one-page network-evidence snapshot showing TLS handshake metadata to controlplane.private.redwood.ai, and the last penetration test executive summary focused on egress behaviour.
- For Acme's higher compliance tiers: we recommend IP allowlist + SNI checks. If Acme chooses SNI-only enforcement, note that TLS 1.3 Encrypted SNI (ESNI) may prevent deep-inspection devices from seeing SNI; in that case allowlisting by IP is the only reliable method.
- Fallback and operational controls: confirm you have a local proxy configured for retry/backoff (we supply SDKs that can expose metrics) and that your firewall team is comfortable returning 503 vs TCP reset semantics. We prefer graceful 503 so Redwood can surface a clear error and automatic retries.

Action items for Redwood to attach to the packet:
1) private-endpoint-acceptance-packet.pdf (combines the IP list, SNI guidance, rotation SLA).
2) network-evidence-sample.txt (handy snippet showing expected TLS SNI and common ciphers).
3) a short on-call contact for emergency unblocking (ops on-call pager).

Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Note: we will redact any customer-identifying flow samples in the final bundle.
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

- Telemetry IPs (stable, low-volume): 198.51.101.21, 198.51.101.22 (/32 each)
